score: Submitted time_log2 = log2(total computation in target-group-operation equivalents), lower is better. All attack work must be justified in proof.md. Ordinary review checks the submitted bound; it does not automatically tighten it.
probability_space: Uniform challenge from the selected profile and fresh independent algorithm coins. The target parameters remain fixed. Reproducible seeds are experimental evidence, not a proof of ideal independent coins.
scope: One classical cold attack on one target. Precomputation is charged in full without amortization over future targets. Quantum algorithms and external advice/oracles with uncharged construction are out of scope.
machine: Scalar AArch64 instruction-equivalent work, with 64-bit general-purpose registers. Arithmetic, logical operations, loads/stores, addressing and control instructions count. Larger arithmetic and data structures must account for their implementation. These are instruction counts, not CPU cycles.
arithmetic: A reference operation costs one group-equivalent unit. Other work costs its justified scalar AArch64 instruction count divided by C. Analytical instruction-equivalent bounds are sufficient; machine code and a production-size run are not required. Do not double-count a reference operation and its implementation.
total_time_includes: randomness and rejection sampling by the attack
parallel_computation: Sum all processors' work, including coordination; elapsed time does not define the score.
nonuniform_advice: Charge construction/search of embedded or stored precomputed results, including parameter-dependent tables. Include advice in peak memory. Public profile constants and algorithm design effort are excluded; embedding searched results in code does not make their construction free.
organizer_work: Challenge generation and organizer review/verification are excluded. Any equivalent work performed by the attack is charged. The attack receives only public inputs and profile constants, never the challenge sampling secret.
memory: Report a reviewed bound in bytes on peak total storage, including code, advice, tables, processor state and retained randomness. Memory has no scalar contribution or tie-break.

claim_fields.time_log2: log2(total computation in target-group-operation equivalents); justify in proof.md
claim_fields.preprocessing_log2: log2(max(1,preprocessing in target-group-operation equivalents)); included in total computation

normalization: Divide charged scalar reference-instruction work by the fixed C for the track. G1 addition uses the batched incomplete affine 6M convention, with S=M and A=0. Pairing inversion use dense Fp12 multiplication. Prices are rounded organizer normalization constants grounded in the pinned measurements; they are not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts.

reference_operations.secp256k1-ecdlp: batched incomplete affine secp256k1 addition, 6M with S=M and A=0
reference_operations.bls12-381-invert-g1: dense Fp12 multiplication, calibrated with pinned blst
reference_operations.bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: batched incomplete affine BLS12-381 G1 addition, 6M with S=M and A=0
reference_operations.bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: dense Fp12 multiplication, calibrated with pinned blst
reference_operations.bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: dense Fp12 multiplication, calibrated with pinned blst
reference_operations.bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: batched incomplete affine BLS12-381 G1 addition, 6M with S=M and A=0
reference_operations.p256-ecdlp: Borrowed secp256k1 reference unit (1,000 instructions); not a P-256 addition price; account actual P-256 work in instructions
